description: Build the cross-agent installer: a NEW zero-dependency Node/TypeScript package under installer/ in the feature-forge repo that installs the feature-forge skill suite into any of five coding agents (claude, codex, copilot, cursor, gemini). Epic agent-agnostic, member 4 of 6. Implementation lands in feature-forge (/home/gary/workspace/feature-forge); these specs/backlog are driven from rauf. The package compiles with tsc (strict + noUncheckedIndexedAccess), tests with node:test (zero runtime deps), and is verified through feature-forge's single gate bash scripts/validate.sh (extended with a hard step 8 that runs npm ci && npm run build && npm test in installer/). Items are ordered strictly bottom-up so every item's whole-package `npm run build` plus its colocated node:test stay green.

items.title: Scaffold installer Node package and shared types (types.ts)
items.description: Create feature-forge's first Node package under installer/. Files: (1) installer/package.json — name "feature-forge", version "0.1.0", type:"module", bin {"feature-forge":"dist/cli.js"}, exports {".":{"types":"./dist/index.d.ts","import":"./dist/index.js"}}, files:["dist","adapters"], engines.node>=18, scripts {build:"tsc -p tsconfig.json", test:"node --test"}, dependencies {} (ZERO runtime deps), devDependencies typescript ^5.4.0 + @types/node ^20.0.0. (2) installer/tsconfig.json — target ES2022, module/moduleResolution NodeNext, outDir dist, rootDir src, declaration true, strict true, noUncheckedIndexedAccess true, esModuleInterop true, skipLibCheck true, include ["src"]. (3) installer/src/types.ts — export EVERY shared type/const from spec 00: AGENT_IDS (const tuple ["claude","codex","copilot","cursor","gemini"]) and AgentId derived from it; Scope, Mode, Subcommand; EXIT + ExitCode; SCHEMA_VERSION=1, FEATURE_FORGE_NS="feature-forge", MANIFEST_PREFIX=".feature-forge."; AgentTarget, ResolveOpts, DetectionResult, ManifestFile, InstallManifest, FileActionKind/FileAction/PlannedAction, AgentReport/RunReport; AGENT_TARGETS (5 rows: claude .claude/skills SKILL.md confirmed; codex .codex/skills; copilot .copilot/skills; cursor .cursor/rules; gemini .gemini/extensions — non-claude rows confidence "best-known"); BUNDLE_REQUIRED_PATHS (common ["skills","scripts/forge-root.sh"], perAgent {gemini:["gemini-extension.json"]}); ErrorCode union, InstallerError; Result<T,E> + ok + err; CliFlags. Named exports only, node: prefix where applicable, JSDoc on public types. Note InstallManifest.featureForgeVersion is string|null (null today). (4) Append to the feature-forge repo-root .gitignore: installer/node_modules/, installer/dist/, installer/adapters/. (5) installer/test/types.test.ts (node:test + node:assert/strict, importing ../dist/types.js) asserting the runtime data-shape invariants tsc cannot catch: AGENT_IDS deep-equals ["claude","codex","copilot","cursor","gemini"] (canonical determinism order, spec 08 §2); Object.keys(AGENT_TARGETS) covers exactly AGENT_IDS; EXIT === {SUCCESS:0,FAILURE:1,USAGE:2}; MANIFEST_PREFIX === ".feature-forge.". Do not create any other src module yet.
acceptanceCriteria: installer/package.json exists with bin {"feature-forge":"dist/cli.js"}, files:["dist","adapters"], engines.node>=18, empty dependencies, and devDeps typescript + @types/node
installer/tsconfig.json has strict:true, noUncheckedIndexedAccess:true, module NodeNext, declaration:true, rootDir src, outDir dist
installer/src/types.ts exports every type/const in spec 00 with the exact names; AgentId is derived from AGENT_IDS; AGENT_TARGETS has exactly the 5 documented rows
feature-forge .gitignore contains installer/node_modules/, installer/dist/, and installer/adapters/
installer/test/types.test.ts asserts AGENT_IDS canonical order, Object.keys(AGENT_TARGETS) === AGENT_IDS, EXIT === {SUCCESS:0,FAILURE:1,USAGE:2}, and MANIFEST_PREFIX === ".feature-forge."
cd installer && npm ci && npm run build && node --test test/types.test.ts passes, emitting dist/types.js and dist/types.d.ts under strict + noUncheckedIndexedAccess
items.notes: All paths under installer/ are relative to the feature-forge repo root (/home/gary/workspace/feature-forge), NOT the rauf repo. This is feature-forge's first-ever Node package (verified: no package.json/tsconfig anywhere). Foundation for every later item — keep type names byte-exact to spec 00 or downstream imports break.

items.title: Implement agent detection map (agent-targets.ts + detect.ts)
items.description: Implement the agent-detection-map surface (spec 02) over the types from item 001. Files: installer/src/agent-targets.ts — re-export AGENT_TARGETS from ./types.js; export resolveRoots(opts?) {home:path.resolve(opts?.home ?? os.homedir()), cwd:path.resolve(opts?.cwd ?? process.cwd())}; destinationFor(target,scope,opts?) = path.resolve(scopeRoot, configDirName, installSubdir, FEATURE_FORGE_NS) where scopeRoot is home for "global" / cwd for "project"; detectAgent(id,opts?):DetectionResult; detectAgents(opts?):DetectionResult[] iterating AGENT_IDS (opts.only scopes to one); formatZeroDetection(results,scope):string naming every probed dir; export interface DetectAgentsOpts extends ResolveOpts {only?:AgentId}. installer/src/detect.ts — probeConfigDir(dir):boolean via fs.statSync(dir).isDirectory() wrapped in try/catch returning false (never mkdir, never throw); cliOnPath(id):boolean advisory only via execFileSync(where|command -v) wrapped to return false on any failure (cursor omitted from CLI_NAMES). Detection signal = config-dir stat ONLY; cliOnPath never gates detected. Pure/total, returns plain values (not Result). Also add the test harness used by later items: installer/test/helpers/sandbox.ts (withSandbox allocating a temp HOME+cwd+source under os.tmpdir() via mkdtemp and tearing down in finally; seedConfigDir(sb,agent,scope) mkdir of the config dir) and installer/test/helpers/fixtures.ts (makeFixtureBundle(sb,agent,skills=["forge-1-prd"]) writing skills/<id>/SKILL.md + scripts/forge-root.sh, plus gemini-extension.json for gemini). Tests: installer/test/agent-targets.test.ts + installer/test/detect.test.ts using node:test + node:assert/strict, importing the built ../dist/*.js.
acceptanceCriteria: agent-targets.ts exports resolveRoots, destinationFor, detectAgent, detectAgents, formatZeroDetection, DetectAgentsOpts, and re-exports AGENT_TARGETS
destinationFor matches the 5-agent x 2-scope table (e.g. claude/global -> <home>/.claude/skills/feature-forge; cursor/project -> <cwd>/.cursor/rules/feature-forge)
Detection is stat-based: with a sandbox HOME where only .claude exists, detectAgents returns detected:true only for claude; probeConfigDir never throws and never creates a dir
Zero-detection: formatZeroDetection names every probed config dir and the run creates no directory; a synthetic 6th AGENT_TARGETS row flows through detectAgents/destinationFor with no function edit
cd installer && npm run build && node --test test/agent-targets.test.ts test/detect.test.ts passes
items.notes: Non-claude rows are 'best-known' (TQ-1/OQ-B) — a path correction is a one-row AGENT_TARGETS edit with no logic change. sandbox.ts/fixtures.ts are reused by items 003,005,007,008,011 — name and locate them exactly as the spec 08 helper layout. Helpers must NOT end in .test.ts so the test glob ignores them.

items.title: Implement source location and content hashing (hash.ts + source.ts)
items.description: Implement the two leaf modules of spec 03 over the types from item 001. installer/src/hash.ts (node:crypto, node:fs, node:path) — sha256File(p):string (64-char hex of file bytes); sha256Tree(dir):string folding a single sha256 over each regular file in SORTED POSIX-relpath order as update(rel)+update('\0')+update(contentHash)+update('\n') — content-only, NEVER mtime, location-invariant; computeSourceHash(bundlePath) = sha256Tree(bundlePath); listBundleFiles(bundlePath):{relpath,sha256}[] sorted by POSIX relpath (same walk as sha256Tree). Internal helpers walkFiles (regular files only, symlinks excluded) and toPosix. installer/src/source.ts (node:fs, node:path, node:url) — LocateBundleOpts {source?}; locateBundle(agent,opts) resolving first existing dir in order [opts.source/<agent>, <installerPkgRoot>/adapters/<agent>, <repoRoot>/adapters/<agent>] (roots derived from import.meta.url, cwd-independent), else err SOURCE_MISSING naming the expected path + remedy; checkIntegrity(bundlePath,agent) using BUNDLE_REQUIRED_PATHS (skills/ non-empty dir + scripts/forge-root.sh, plus gemini-extension.json for gemini) — must NOT require .claude-plugin/plugin.json or epic-manifest.py (IR-1/OQ-A); listBundleSkills(bundlePath):string[] enumerating skills/* DIRECTORY NAMES only (never opens a skill file); locateSource(agent,opts):Result<LocatedSource{root,sourceHash,skills,files}> running locateBundle -> checkIntegrity -> fingerprint, returning the same SOURCE_MISSING/SOURCE_INVALID errors. Result<T,E> returns, no throw for expected errors. Tests: installer/test/hash.test.ts + installer/test/source.test.ts (relocation-invariant + mtime-touch-stable digests; content edit changes digest; SOURCE_MISSING/SOURCE_INVALID name the offending path; checkIntegrity passes without plugin.json) using fixtures.ts from item 002.
acceptanceCriteria: hash.ts exports sha256File, sha256Tree, computeSourceHash, listBundleFiles; source.ts exports locateBundle, checkIntegrity, listBundleSkills, locateSource, LocateBundleOpts, LocatedSource

sha256Tree/computeSourceHash return the same digest for two copies of an identical tree at different paths and after an mtime-only touch, but a different digest after a content edit (content-defined, OQ-4)
locateBundle resolves --source before packaged/in-repo candidates and returns err SOURCE_MISSING (naming the expected path + remedy) when no candidate exists

checkIntegrity returns SOURCE_INVALID naming the missing path when skills/ is empty, scripts/forge-root.sh is absent, or (gemini) gemini-extension.json is absent; it does NOT require plugin.json or epic-manifest.py
cd installer && npm run build && node --test test/hash.test.ts test/source.test.ts passes
items.notes: Verified ground truth: every adapters/<agent>/ bundle has skills/ (11 dirs), references/, scripts/forge-root.sh, agents/; gemini adds gemini-extension.json. Only the BUNDLE_REQUIRED_PATHS subset is gated. POSIX-normalize relpaths before hashing so digests match on Windows and POSIX (C-6). hash.ts and source.ts import only types (001); the dependsOn 002 preserves the strict bottom-up build order, not an import.

items.title: Implement rauf provisioning (rauf.ts) and the library barrel (index.ts)
items.description: Implement spec 06 plus the library barrel from spec 01 §4. installer/src/rauf.ts (node:child_process only, for the read-only preflight) — export const RAUF_PIN = "rauf@0.6.0"; export type RegistryQuery = (coordinate:string) => Result<string>; export function preflightRauf(opts?:{skip?:boolean; query?:RegistryQuery}):Result<{raufPin:string|null}> — when opts.skip return ok({raufPin:null}) with NO network call; else run query (default defaultRegistryQuery) and on success return ok({raufPin:RAUF_PIN}), on failure return err(raufUnresolvableError()); internal defaultRegistryQuery via spawnSync('npm',['view',coordinate,'version'],{encoding:'utf8',timeout:30000,windowsHide:true}) returning ok(trimmed stdout) only on exit 0 + non-empty stdout, else err RAUF_UNRESOLVABLE (also on spawn throw / npm absent); internal raufUnresolvableError() returning the FIXED spec-06 §6 message with RAUF_PIN substituted. preflightRauf NEVER throws and performs NO filesystem write. installer/src/index.ts — barrel re-exporting { AGENT_TARGETS, resolveRoots, destinationFor, detectAgent, detectAgents, formatZeroDetection } from ./agent-targets.js, { RAUF_PIN } from ./rauf.js, and the spec-00 types (AgentId, AgentTarget, DetectionResult, ResolveOpts, Scope, Mode, InstallManifest, PlannedAction, RunReport) from ./types.js. Add installer/test/helpers/registry.ts exporting resolvableRegistry (()=>ok('0.6.0')), unresolvableRegistry (()=>err RAUF_UNRESOLVABLE), neverCalledRegistry (throws if called). Test installer/test/rauf.test.ts: skip -> ok{raufPin:null} and query never invoked; resolvable stub -> ok{raufPin:RAUF_PIN}; unresolvable stub -> err RAUF_UNRESOLVABLE carrying the production fixed message regardless of the stub's message; no fs write.
acceptanceCriteria: rauf.ts exports RAUF_PIN === "rauf@0.6.0", the RegistryQuery type, and preflightRauf
preflightRauf({skip:true}) returns ok({raufPin:null}) and makes no network call (an injected throwing query is never invoked)

preflightRauf with a resolvable injected query returns ok({raufPin:RAUF_PIN}); with an err query it returns err({code:"RAUF_UNRESOLVABLE"}) carrying the fixed spec-06 message regardless of the stub's message
src/index.ts re-exports exactly the agent-detection-map surface + RAUF_PIN + the listed types; preflightRauf performs no filesystem write and never throws

preflightRauf only records RAUF_PIN and performs no filesystem write or runner-selection lock — it does not preclude an alternate loop runner (REQ-RAUF-05); the unresolvable and --skip-rauf paths still install skills
cd installer && npm run build && node --test test/rauf.test.ts passes
items.notes: DESIGNED failure mode, not a bug: rauf is not npm-publishable yet (IR-2), so the real `npm view rauf@0.6.0` 404s -> RAUF_UNRESOLVABLE. Skills still install; the run exits non-zero; --skip-rauf defers it. All tests use the injectable RegistryQuery mock (no real network). index.ts compiles only after agent-targets.ts (002) and rauf.ts (this item) exist — that is why the barrel lives here.

items.title: Implement install manifest and uninstall policy (manifest.ts)
items.description:
Implement spec 05: installer/src/manifest.ts (node:fs, node:path; imports types from ./types.js and destinationFor from ./agent-targets.js). Exports: manifestPath(agent,scope,opts?) = path.join(dirname(destinationFor(AGENT_TARGETS[agent],scope,opts)), `${MANIFEST_PREFIX}${scope}.json`) — the hidden parent-sibling of the namespace dir, identical for copy and symlink; readManifest(p):Result — ENOENT -> ok(null); read error -> MANIFEST_CORRUPT; JSON.parse wrapped in try/catch -> MANIFEST_CORRUPT; failed shape validation -> MANIFEST_CORRUPT; writeManifest(p,m):Result — atomic write (

.tmp then renameSync), mkdir -p parent, EACCES/EPERM -> WRITE_DENIED, cleans up the temp file on failure; buildManifest(args):InstallManifest — featureForgeVersion ALWAYS null (OQ-A/IR-1; C-3 forbids synthesizing one), preserve previous.installedAt on update else now, updatedAt always now, sort files+skills, include link only when provided, files:[] in symlink mode, injectable now clock; planUninstall(manifest):Result — pure, manifest-only, all-"remove": copy mode one {relpath,action:"remove"} per files[].path in recorded order, symlink mode the single {relpath:".",action:"remove"}; export BuildManifestArgs. Internal validateManifest checking schemaVersion===1, agent/scope/mode enums, required fields, files[] entries, and the cross-field invariant symlink => link present / copy => link absent. No throw for expected errors. Test installer/test/manifest.test.ts: manifestPath parent-sibling formula; readManifest ok(null)/MANIFEST_CORRUPT (bad JSON + schemaVersion mismatch); writeManifest atomic + WRITE_DENIED on a read-only dir; buildManifest null version + installedAt preservation + symlink files:[]; planUninstall copy vs symlink shapes.
acceptanceCriteria: manifest.ts exports manifestPath, readManifest, writeManifest, buildManifest, planUninstall, BuildManifestArgs (named exports), importing all shared types from ./types.js
manifestPath('claude','global',{home}) -> <home>/.claude/skills/.feature-forge.global.json (parent-sibling; same formula for project with .project.json)

readManifest returns ok(null) for ENOENT, err MANIFEST_CORRUPT for invalid JSON and for a schemaVersion mismatch (JSON.parse inside try/catch); writeManifest writes atomically (.tmp then rename) and returns WRITE_DENIED on a permission failure

buildManifest sets featureForgeVersion:null always, preserves previous.installedAt on update, sorts files/skills, emits files:[] in symlink mode; planUninstall returns the all-remove copy plan (per files[].path) and the single {relpath:'.',action:'remove'} symlink plan
cd installer && npm run build && node --test test/manifest.test.ts passes
items.notes: planUninstall owns the removal POLICY (which paths); the safe EXECUTION (containment-checked removal, empty-dir prune, link-safe unlink, manifest-last deletion) is apply() in item 008 — do NOT implement an applyUninstall here. manifest.ts's only real import is destinationFor from agent-targets (002) + types (001); it does NOT import plan.ts. The dependsOn 003 keeps the strict linear build order — 003 exports nothing manifest imports, and the 002 import is reached transitively (005 -> 003 -> 002).

items.title: Implement sandboxed filesystem primitives (fsutil.ts)
items.description: Implement spec 04 §7: installer/src/fsutil.ts (node:fs/promises, node:path, node:os; imports Result/ok/err from ./types.js). Exports: resolveWithin(root,...segs):Result<string> — base=path.resolve(root); target=path.resolve(base,...segs); rel=path.relative(base,target); inside iff rel==="" OR (!rel.startsWith("..") && !path.isAbsolute(rel)); else err PATH_ESCAPE (naming target+base+remedy). MUST be called before any write/delete. copyDir(src,dest):Promise<Result<void>> — mkdir -p dirname(dest) then fs.cp(src,dest,{recursive:true,force:true,dereference:false}); EACCES/EPERM -> WRITE_DENIED. symlinkDir(target,linkPath):Promise<Result<{mode:"symlink"|"copy"}>> — on Windows OR any symlink syscall failure, fall back to copyDir and return mode:"copy"; else fs.symlink(target,linkPath,"dir") and return mode:"symlink". removePath(p):Promise<Result<void>> — lstat (NOT stat): symbolic link -> fs.unlink(p) (link only, never the target); real directory -> fs.rm(p,{recursive:true,force:true}); real file -> fs.unlink(p); ENOENT -> ok (idempotent). removeEmptyDirsWithin(startDir,stopRoot):Promise<Result<void>> — assert containment via resolveWithin, then prune empty dirs from startDir upward while cur!==stopRoot && cur within stopRoot, halting on the first non-empty dir (never removes a non-empty dir or stopRoot itself). isWindows():boolean = os.platform()==="win32". Internal toWriteError mapping EACCES/EPERM -> WRITE_DENIED, else UNEXPECTED. No throw for expected errors. Test installer/test/fsutil.test.ts: resolveWithin accepts in-root and rejects ../absolute with PATH_ESCAPE before any write; removePath on a symlinked dir unlinks the link and leaves the target tree byte-intact; removeEmptyDirsWithin prunes empties but halts on a dir holding an untracked file.
acceptanceCriteria: fsutil.ts exports resolveWithin, copyDir, symlinkDir, removePath, removeEmptyDirsWithin, isWindows (named exports)
resolveWithin rejects '..'/absolute escapes with err PATH_ESCAPE (before any fs op) and accepts in-root segments; a crafted segment cannot resolve outside root

removePath uses lstat: on a symlink it unlinks the link only and the link target tree is byte-for-byte intact afterward; on a real dir it removes recursively; on a missing path it returns ok (idempotent)
removeEmptyDirsWithin prunes empty dirs up to but excluding stopRoot and halts on the first non-empty dir (never removes a non-empty dir)
cd installer && npm run build && node --test test/fsutil.test.ts passes
items.notes: These are the single place REQ-SEC-01/02/03 are enforced — every mutation in apply() (008) routes through them. resolveWithin uses path.relative + the '..' prefix test (a bare string startsWith would false-pass /root-evil). fsutil only needs types (001); the dependsOn 005 is to preserve the strict build order, not an import.

items.title: Implement the pure planner (plan.ts)
items.description: Implement the pure planner of spec 04 (the dry-run = real-run engine): installer/src/plan.ts. Imports types from ./types.js, sha256File/listBundleFiles from ./hash.js, locateSource/LocatedSource from ./source.js, readManifest/manifestPath/planUninstall from ./manifest.js, isWindows from ./fsutil.js. Exports: PlanContext interface; classifyFile(relpath,srcHash,destHash?,manifestHash?,force):FileActionKind implementing the 7-row table — destHash undefined -> create; destHash===srcHash -> unchanged; else if manifestHash!==undefined && destHash===manifestHash -> overwrite (clean prior, source changed, no --force, REQ-IDEM-03); else force?overwrite:skip-modified (drifted tracked OR untracked differing, REQ-IDEM-02); planInstall(ctx):Result<PlannedAction>; planUpdate(ctx):Result<PlannedAction> = planInstall decisions PLUS orphanRemovals (paths in priorManifest.files absent from source.files -> remove; manifest-scoped only); symlink-mode produces a single synthetic FileAction for relpath "." ({create | unchanged if prior link target === source.root | skip-modified/overwrite if prior exists}); plan(subcommand,ctx) dispatcher routing install->planInstall, update->planUpdate, uninstall->planUninstall(ctx.priorManifest) (empty-files plan when priorManifest null); resolveMode(wantSymlink,windows=isWindows()):Mode = wantSymlink && !windows ? "symlink" : "copy". The planner performs ZERO filesystem writes and ZERO network calls (it MAY read destination bytes + the prior manifest). A null/invalid ctx.source yields the SOURCE_MISSING/SOURCE_INVALID err. Test installer/test/plan.test.ts: every classifyFile row; resolveMode (symlink off Windows, copy on win32); orphan removal is manifest-scoped (an untracked file is never planned for removal); the same PlannedAction object would be handed to apply on a real run.
acceptanceCriteria: plan.ts exports PlanContext, classifyFile, planInstall, planUpdate, plan, resolveMode

classifyFile returns each documented row: absent dest -> create; D===S -> unchanged; clean prior + changed source -> overwrite (no --force); drifted tracked -> skip-modified (overwrite under force); untracked differing -> skip-modified
planUpdate emits remove only for prior-manifest paths absent from the current source (manifest-scoped); an untracked file is never planned for removal; symlink mode yields a single relpath '.' action
resolveMode returns 'symlink' off Windows when wantSymlink and 'copy' on win32; plan() performs zero writes and zero network calls
cd installer && npm run build && node --test test/plan.test.ts passes
items.notes: Row 3 (S===D -> unchanged) wins over rows 2/4 — compute D and compare to S first. The planner is the single place idempotency/conflict decisions are made (once), so dry-run and real run can never drift. Imports from hash(003), source(003), manifest(005), fsutil(006) — all already built.

items.title: Implement the apply engine (apply.ts)
items.description: Implement the executor of spec 04 §5: installer/src/apply.ts exporting apply(planned:PlannedAction, ctx:ApplyContext):Promise<AgentReport> and the ApplyContext interface. Imports types from ./types.js, sha256File from ./hash.js, fsutil primitives (resolveWithin, copyDir, symlinkDir, removePath, removeEmptyDirsWithin) from ./fsutil.js, buildManifest/writeManifest from ./manifest.js. apply NEVER throws for expected errors — a failure returns AgentReport{ok:false,error}. Copy flow: walk planned.files in order; resolveWithin(agentRoot,destination,relpath) for each (PATH_ESCAPE aborts this agent only); create/overwrite -> ensure parent dir + copy source bytes + record sha256File(dest); remove -> removePath; unchanged/skip-modified -> no write; after the loop write the manifest via buildManifest+writeManifest UNLESS every action was unchanged (no-op short-circuit -> manifest NOT rewritten, updatedAt preserved). Symlink flow: resolveWithin the link path; removePath any prior; symlinkDir(source.root,destination); record files:[] (no sha256) + link.target + mode ("copy" if the fallback fired). Remove flow (uninstall): copy -> removePath each recorded file + removeEmptyDirsWithin(destination,agentRoot) + delete the manifest file LAST; symlink -> removePath the link (lstat+unlink, never recurse into the adapters/ target) + delete the manifest. Gemini has NO special branch — gemini-extension.json is just another file in source.files. Build the InstallManifest with featureForgeVersion:null. Test installer/test/apply.test.ts (using sandbox.ts + fixtures.ts): copy install writes files on disk + manifest; symlink install creates a link + mode:'symlink' + link.target; a WRITE_DENIED via an injected throwing write seam -> ok:false and manifest NOT written; gemini copy lands a parseable gemini-extension.json at the destination.
acceptanceCriteria: apply.ts exports apply and ApplyContext; apply returns an AgentReport and never throws for expected errors
Copy mode: planned create files exist on disk afterward with a recorded sha256; an all-unchanged plan performs zero writes and does not rewrite the manifest (updatedAt preserved)

Symlink mode (off Windows) creates a real symlink whose target is the source bundle and records mode:'symlink' + link.target with per-file sha256 omitted; uninstall unlinks the link and leaves the target tree intact

A write-denied destination yields AgentReport{ok:false,error:WRITE_DENIED} without throwing and the manifest is not written; a gemini copy lands a valid parseable gemini-extension.json with no gemini-specific branch
cd installer && npm run build && node --test test/apply.test.ts passes
items.notes: apply() executes the all-remove plan from planUninstall (005) — there is no separate applyUninstall. Atomicity posture: on a mid-loop write failure the manifest is NOT written, so an idempotent re-run heals the partial install (already-written files hash-match -> unchanged). Test apply directly with a hand-built ApplyContext + a fixture LocatedSource (unit tier); full-CLI e2e is item 011.

items.title: Implement the run reporter (report.ts + formatError)
items.description: Implement spec 07 §3.5/§3.6 reporter: installer/src/report.ts (pure, no I/O; imports types from ./types.js). Export renderReport(report:RunReport, opts:{json:boolean}):string — when opts.json return JSON.stringify(report) (same RunReport data, the machine surface for OS-matrix consumers); else render human text: a header line `${subcommand} (${scope}, ${mode})${dryRun?' — dry-run':''}`, then per agent a block, then a final `Summary: N ok, N failed (exit X)` line. Per-agent block: for list, decode the synthetic status rows (relpath-encoded detected:/installed:/up-to-date:) into one `${agent}: detected|not detected  <status>` line; for a failed agent, `${agent}: FAILED — ${error.code}` then an indented formatError(error) line; for an ok agent, `${agent}: ok` then indented `${actionVerb(action)} ${relpath}` per file, plus a `rauf default runner pinned: <pin>` line when raufPin is set. Export actionVerb(kind) mapping create/overwrite/skip-modified/unchanged/remove to human verbs. Export formatError(e:InstallerError):string composing `<message> — path: <path> — remedy: <remedy>`, falling back to a per-code DEFAULT_REMEDY map (USAGE, SOURCE_MISSING, SOURCE_INVALID, LOCALLY_MODIFIED, WRITE_DENIED, PATH_ESCAPE, RAUF_UNRESOLVABLE, MANIFEST_CORRUPT) when e.remedy is absent. (formatError may live in report.ts or a sibling report-errors.ts.) Test installer/test/report.test.ts: renderReport({json:true}) round-trips to a RunReport via JSON.parse; the human form names path + remedy on a failure; the list line decodes the status rows; every actionVerb branch is covered.
acceptanceCriteria: report.ts exports renderReport({json}) and formatError; renderReport(report,{json:true}) returns parseable JSON deep-equal to the RunReport
Human form includes the header, per-agent ok/FAILED blocks with per-file action verbs, and the final 'Summary: N ok, N failed (exit X)' line
A failed agent's line is rendered via formatError naming the path and a remedy (using the per-code DEFAULT_REMEDY fallback when the error omits one)
The list subcommand renders a 'detected/installed/up-to-date' line decoded from the synthetic status rows
cd installer && npm run build && node --test test/report.test.ts passes
items.notes: report.ts is pure (returns strings; the caller in cli.ts writes them). It only needs types (001); dependsOn 008 keeps the strict build order. The --json output IS the shell surface agent-detection-map consumers read (REQ-DET-05). DEFAULT_REMEDY is intentionally Partial over ErrorCode — UNEXPECTED is surfaced via the cli.ts boundary message (item 010, spec 07 §3.1/§4), not formatError, so it has no DEFAULT_REMEDY entry (spec 07 §3.6).

items.title: Implement CLI entry and dispatch (cli.ts)
items.description: Implement the orchestration layer of spec 07: installer/src/cli.ts. Imports detection (02), locateSource (03), plan/apply/resolveMode (04/07), readManifest/manifestPath/planUninstall (05), preflightRauf/RAUF_PIN (06), renderReport (09). Define the single CLI_SPEC (SUBCOMMANDS install/update/uninstall/list with aliases add/remove/ls; FLAGS agent(-a),global(-g),symlink,force,dry-run,yes(-y),json,skip-rauf,source[hidden],help(-h),version). Export: parseCliArgs(argv):Result<ParsedCli> via node:util.parseArgs — resolve aliases, reject unknown subcommand/flag/agent and a parseArgs throw as USAGE; mapErrorToExit(err):ExitCode (USAGE->2 else 1); helpText():string generated from CLI_SPEC (hides --source); the CliEnv interface {home?,cwd?,registry?,platform?}; runCli(argv,env?):Promise<RunReport> — the testable core that threads env.home/cwd into detection/destinationFor/manifest calls, env.registry into preflightRauf, env.platform into resolveMode, and returns the assembled RunReport WITHOUT touching process; main(argv):Promise<ExitCode> — help/version precedence before subcommand requirement, boundary try/catch turning any UNEXPECTED throw into a one-line stderr message (never a bare stack) and EXIT.FAILURE, returns report.exitCode; plus the entry shim calling main(process.argv.slice(2)). Internal runMutation/runOneAgent/finishAgent (per-agent isolation: one agent's failure -> ok:false AgentReport, loop continues; rauf preflight runs ONCE for install/update, skipped under --dry-run/--skip-rauf; run exitCode FAILURE if any agent failed OR the preflight failed) and runList/listOneAgent (read-only: detected/installed/up-to-date via readManifest + locateSource().sourceHash, NO network/apply). No stdin read anywhere (-y is accepted, never gates flow). Add installer/test/helpers/run.ts exporting runCli2(argv,sb,opts) wrapping runCli with the sandbox roots + resolvableRegistry default + optional platform. Test installer/test/cli.test.ts: alias resolution; unknown subcommand/flag/agent -> USAGE/exit 2; --help and install --help print help/exit 0; bare invocation prints help to stderr/exit 2; --version prints the version/exit 0.
acceptanceCriteria: cli.ts exports parseCliArgs, main, runCli, CliEnv, mapErrorToExit, helpText, SUBCOMMANDS, FLAGS; runCli threads home/cwd/registry/platform and returns a RunReport without touching process

parseCliArgs resolves add->install, remove->uninstall, ls->list; unknown subcommand, unknown flag, and unknown --agent each return USAGE and mapErrorToExit gives EXIT.USAGE (2); every other code gives EXIT.FAILURE (1)

main(['--help']) and main(['install','--help']) print helpText and return 0; main([]) prints help to stderr and returns 2; main(['--version']) prints the version and returns 0; helpText lists every non-hidden flag/subcommand and omits --source
test/helpers/run.ts exports runCli2; no code path reads stdin (-y is accepted and shown in help)
cd installer && npm run build && node --test test/cli.test.ts passes; node dist/cli.js --help runs under plain Node >=18
items.notes: This wires every prior module together — it is the last src module before the integration suite. The rauf preflight is RUN-LEVEL not per-agent: on failure every agent's skill install still succeeds (AgentReport.ok stays true) while the run exitCode becomes FAILURE. runCli's injectable env is the hermetic-test seam item 011 relies on.

items.title: Author the integration/e2e behavioral suite + coverage checklist
items.description: Author the hermetic integration suite of spec 08 §5 driving runCli2 (from test/helpers/run.ts) against a temp HOME via withSandbox, makeFixtureBundle sources, and a mock RegistryQuery — no real ~ and no network. Every test wraps its body in withSandbox for guaranteed teardown; tests import the built ../dist/*.js. Cover the matrix (group into focused e2e-*.test.ts files): dry-run = real-run (dest byte-identical before/after the dry-run AND deepEqual of dry vs real per-agent actions); idempotency (re-run all-unchanged, zero writes, manifest updatedAt unchanged); update reconcile add/change/remove + multi-skill scale (all skill dirs land, manifest.skills updated) + manifest-scoped orphan removal (untracked sibling survives); skip-modified + --force; uninstall exactness (untracked file inside + an unrelated file outside the namespace survive; manifest gone); symlink link + uninstall-unlinks-with-target-intact + Windows-always-copies via the platform inject; source integrity / partial failure (claude valid + gemini SOURCE_MISSING/SOURCE_INVALID, exit FAILURE, no partial gemini install, claude still succeeds); gemini outcome (valid gemini-extension.json at dest); rauf preflight 3 cases (resolvable records raufPin / unresolvable: skills still install + exit non-zero + fixed message / --skip-rauf: registry never called) + RAUF-04 idempotent+reversible; path sandbox (PATH_ESCAPE before any write); list status + no-network (neverCalledRegistry never invoked); synthetic-agent-row scale. Add installer/test/coverage.test.ts asserting every public function in specs 02–07 is defined+reachable, every FileActionKind (create/overwrite/skip-modified/unchanged/remove) and every ErrorCode is produced by >=1 test (WRITE_DENIED via a deterministic injected throwing-write seam, not a platform-gated chmod), and both modes (copy/symlink) + both scopes (project/global) are exercised.
acceptanceCriteria: The dry-run = real-run test asserts byte-identical destination before/after the dry-run AND deepEqual of dry vs real per-agent actions

Idempotency, update reconcile (add/change/remove + multi-skill + manifest-scoped orphan), skip-modified+force, uninstall exactness, symlink (link + uninstall target-intact + Windows-copy via platform inject), source-integrity/partial-failure, gemini outcome, rauf 3 cases + RAUF-04, path sandbox, and list no-network are each covered by a passing test

coverage.test.ts asserts every public fn in 02–07 is reachable, every FileActionKind and every ErrorCode is produced by >=1 test (WRITE_DENIED via an injected throwing-write seam), and both modes + both scopes are exercised (authoritative public-function list: 08-testing-strategy.md §6)
Every test is hermetic: a temp HOME under os.tmpdir() via withSandbox, a fixture bundle via makeFixtureBundle, and a mock RegistryQuery — no real ~, no real npm view, no network
cd installer && npm run build && npm test runs the whole node:test suite with 0 failures
items.notes: The matrix areas are independent test files sharing the same helpers and one verification step (npm test) — a good fit for agentDelegation. Keep each subtask's files disjoint. Determinism: iteration order follows AGENT_IDS; timestamps asserted by ISO shape, never value. node --test runs the test/*.test.ts glob; helpers (non-.test.ts) are imported, never auto-run.

agentDelegation.strategy: Each sub-agent authors one disjoint group of e2e-*.test.ts files under installer/test/, all driving runCli2 + withSandbox + makeFixtureBundle + a mock RegistryQuery. They share the helpers (read-only) but write different test files, so there are no write conflicts; the whole suite is verified once by `npm test`.
subtasks: Author installer/test/e2e-install.test.ts covering dry-run=real-run (byte-identical dest + deepEqual actions), idempotency (all-unchanged/zero-writes/updatedAt-unchanged), and SEC-01 positive containment.

Author installer/test/e2e-update-uninstall.test.ts covering update reconcile (add/change/remove + multi-skill scale + manifest-scoped orphan), skip-modified+force, and uninstall exactness (untracked inside + unrelated outside survive, manifest gone).

Author installer/test/e2e-symlink-source.test.ts covering symlink link+uninstall-target-intact + Windows-copy via platform inject, source-integrity/partial-failure (claude ok + gemini SOURCE_MISSING/INVALID, exit FAILURE), gemini outcome, and the PATH_ESCAPE path sandbox.

Author installer/test/e2e-rauf-list-scale.test.ts (rauf 3 cases + RAUF-04, list status + no-network) and installer/test/coverage.test.ts (every public fn reachable, every FileActionKind + ErrorCode incl. WRITE_DENIED via injected throwing-write seam, both modes + both scopes).

items.title: Wire the installer into the feature-forge gate (validate.sh step 8)
items.description:
Extend feature-forge's scripts/validate.sh with a new TOP-LEVEL hard step that builds and tests the installer through the single C-2 gate (the installer is the deliverable C-2 must verify, and there is NO rauf pnpm gate for this feature). Insert the step immediately BEFORE the final summary block (the `if [ "$ERRORS" -eq 0 ]; then ... "All checks passed!" ... else ... "$ERRORS error(s) found."; exit 1; fi` block at the end of the 204-line file). Use the file's existing spaced failure-accumulation idiom `ERRORS=$((ERRORS + 1))` (with spaces). The step:

  echo ""
  echo "Building + testing the cross-agent installer..."
  if command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if ( cd "$REPO_ROOT/installer" && npm ci --silent && npm run build --silent && npm test ); then
      echo "PASS: installer build + node:test suite"
    else
      echo "FAIL: installer build/test (see above)"
      ERRORS=$((ERRORS + 1))
    fi
  else
    echo "FAIL: node/npm not found — required to build + test the installer (install Node >= 18)"
    ERRORS=$((ERRORS + 1))
  fi

npm absence is a HARD ERROR (not a pytest-style soft skip). REPO_ROOT is the existing variable validate.sh already resolves. Also confirm the feature-forge .gitignore still carries installer/node_modules/, installer/dist/, installer/adapters/ (added in item 001); add any that are missing. Do not modify any other validate.sh step.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/validate.sh has a new top-level step inserted before the final summary block that runs `(cd "$REPO_ROOT/installer" && npm ci --silent && npm run build --silent && npm test)` and increments ERRORS with the spaced `ERRORS=$((ERRORS + 1))` form on failure
npm absence is treated as a hard ERROR (ERRORS incremented), not a soft skip
.gitignore carries installer/node_modules/, installer/dist/, and installer/adapters/
bash scripts/validate.sh exits 0 end-to-end with the installer present (the C-2 feature gate is green)
items.notes: This is THE single 'is it green?' command for the whole feature (C-2/C-4) — downstream consumers (forge-rauf-loop-default, packaging-docs-ci) rely on it. The npm ci in step 8 auto-provisions the Node toolchain (typescript + @types/node only) — no manual setup (C-4). Placed after item 011 so the full build+test suite is in place and the gate runs green.

items.title: Fix epic contract V-001: correct this feature's consumes coordinate
items.description: Epic-level contract fix (V-001 / CHECK-E06), in the RAUF repo (NOT feature-forge). The cross-agent-installer feature currently declares its `consumes` as `agent-cli-registry`, but it should be the published rauf bin coordinate that this feature provisions and downstream forge-rauf-loop-default invokes (per spec 06 / RAUF_PIN = rauf@0.6.0). Correct it in lockstep in BOTH files so they never drift: (1) specs/agent-agnostic/epic-manifest.json — the features[] entry whose name is "cross-agent-installer": update its consumes array entry from agent-cli-registry to the published rauf bin coordinate. (2) specs/agent-agnostic/EPIC.md — the cross-agent-installer Contracts/Consumes section: update the same coordinate to match. Read both files first to confirm the exact current wording and the canonical rauf-bin coordinate used elsewhere in the epic. After editing, validate epic-manifest.json with `python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('specs/agent-agnostic/epic-manifest.json'))"` and confirm the EPIC.md section reads consistently. Do not touch any other feature's contract.
acceptanceCriteria: specs/agent-agnostic/epic-manifest.json: the cross-agent-installer features[] entry's consumes no longer lists agent-cli-registry and instead lists the published rauf bin coordinate
specs/agent-agnostic/EPIC.md: the cross-agent-installer Consumes section names the same rauf bin coordinate, matching the manifest in lockstep
No other feature's consumes/exposes entries are changed in either file
python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('specs/agent-agnostic/epic-manifest.json'))" exits 0 (valid JSON)
items.notes: Independent of the installer code — these edits live in the rauf repo's epic specs, not feature-forge. Must be applied to BOTH files in lockstep (CHECK-E06) or the epic verify will re-flag the drift. Validate the JSON before finishing (appending/editing JSON via Edit has dropped closing braces before — json.load guards against that).
